actions.name: Endorse a statement (k of the room)
actions.summary: The room ratifies a sentence: k of its members sign it with their room identities. Nothing goes to a chain; the signed decision lives in the room's log.

fields.name: text
fields.means: the sentence the room ratifies, verbatim

steps.does: Room → + → Statement → Endorse with Threshold, types the text and proposes. The hosted module builds the driver over the room's CURRENT members — their Ed25519 identities from the membership fold — with k = min(2, members). The proposal publishes its policy, the effect, and the signing context: environment 'room', account = the room's topic, slot = the intent id, expiry = now + MUSTER_INTENT_TTL_S (7 days by default). The intent id is content-addressed from the effect and the policy.

Re-derives the materialization from the logged effect — dCBOR ['muster.threshold.v1', 'muster.effect.statement.v1', {text}] — and approves in-app: the keystore signs it with the member's Ed25519 room identity and signs the attestation over P with the same key. The driver counts a signature only if it verifies under one of the roster's keys; the fold reaches executable at k. A member may Deny instead: named, informational, the threshold unchanged.
steps.signs: an Ed25519 signature by the member's room identity (their encryption identity's Ed25519 key, held in the keystore) over the materialization: the dCBOR array [serialization domain, schema id, {field: value…}] (CDE map order, shortest integers); plus a muster attestation by the same key over P = (context, the materialization, the provenance record)

steps.does: Executable is the end: agreement is final in the room. coordinate_submit on it answers 'not-onchain': a room family has no settlement, and the card reads '✓ Endorsed — a signed group decision. Nothing settles on-chain.'

refusals.what: an endorsement by a key that is not on the roster
refusals.why: the driver identifies no roster member for it; it never counts, and the live path answers 'rejected'

refusals.what: an endorsement over bytes other than the re-derived materialization (a changed text, another schema)
refusals.why: invariant 1: the statement selects its own schema, so a transfer's bytes and a statement's never match; a tampered effect is refused by the driver's conformance check

refusals.what: an in-app approval after the intent's expiry
an in-app approval when an input has no source record
an attestation that does not verify over the P every member re-derives
refusals.why: graded rejected: the approval does not count
a room family has no settlement: 'not-onchain'

actions.ui: Room → + → Statement → Endorse with Threshold → text → Propose; card → Approve or Deny; the ready box reads '✓ Endorsed — a signed group decision. Nothing settles on-chain.'

claims.claim: Only a valid Ed25519 signature by a room member over the re-derived bytes counts
The decision never leaves the room: no chain, no RPC, no module
The store node relaying the sealed room sees when events pass and on which topic, not what they say
k distinct members: the fold dedups by the name in the event key, so it relies on members publishing under their own names

unverified: The room's fold counts one approval per contributor NAME in the event key (intent/<id>/sig/<who>/<round>), not per verifying key: a valid signature by one member, published a second time under another name, counts twice and the intent reaches 'executable' with one signer (confirmed by a scratch run against the threshold driver while writing this corpus; no repo test covers it). A room family has no settlement to re-check the signers, so for it the room's count is the outcome. Honest clients publish under the recovered name (coordination/live.nim).
k = min(2, members) is how nim-lib/muster_module.nim (roomDriver) builds the hosted driver; the tests build their own rosters.

actions.name: Endorse a statement (every member)
actions.summary: Every member of the room must sign. 'unanimous' is the k = n threshold; it is not a founding kind — a room admits it only by approving an add-driver proposal first.

fields.name: text
fields.means: the sentence the room ratifies, verbatim

steps.does: Selects Unanimous in the Statement picker — offered only once the room has admitted it; before that the button reads '＋ Propose unanimous' and proposes the add-driver instead. coordinate_set_policy refuses a kind the room has not admitted ('policy not admitted in this room'). The proposal publishes its policy, the effect, and the signing context: environment 'room', account = the room's topic, slot = the intent id, expiry = now + MUSTER_INTENT_TTL_S (7 days by default). The intent id is content-addressed from the effect and the policy.

As a threshold statement, with k = the roster size: every current member's Ed25519 endorsement is needed. The roster is the room's current membership, so a member admitted before the last approval raises n.
steps.signs: an Ed25519 signature by the member's room identity (their encryption identity's Ed25519 key, held in the keystore) over the materialization: the dCBOR array ['muster.threshold.v1', schema id, {field: value…}] (CDE map order, shortest integers); plus a muster attestation by the same key over P = (context, the materialization, the provenance record)

steps.does: Executable is the end. coordinate_submit on it answers 'not-onchain': a room family has no settlement, and the card reads '✓ Endorsed — a signed group decision. Nothing settles on-chain.'

refusals.what: using unanimous before the room admitted it
refusals.why: it is not a founding kind and is not among the room's kinds until an add-driver for it is approved; coordinate_set_policy refuses a kind not among them, and the composer offers the add-driver instead

refusals.what: an endorsement by a key not on the roster

actions.ui: Room → + → Statement → Endorse with Unanimous (shown as '＋ Propose unanimous' until the room admits it) → text → Propose; card → Approve.

claims.claim: Unanimous is the threshold driver with k = n over the room's roster
Admission gates what an honest client composes; the fold itself resolves 'unanimous' whether or not the room admitted it
k distinct members: the fold dedups by the name in the event key

unverified: governance_test proves roomDriverKinds admits 'unanimous' after an approved add-driver; that coordinate_set_policy refuses it before is from reading nim-lib/muster_module.nim (musterCoordinateSetPolicy).
That the fold does not check admission, and that n follows the current membership, are from reading nim-lib/muster_module.nim (roomDriver, driverForPolicy); no test covers either.

A room family has no settlement to re-check the signers, so for it the room's count is the outcome. Honest clients publish under the recovered name (coordination/live.nim).

actions.name: Admit a new policy into the room (driver-as-proposal)
actions.summary: What a room can do grows by proposal, not a compile-time list (invariant 6): the room endorses an add-driver intent naming a kind, and once it is approved the kind is admitted — if this client has it.

fields.name: kind
fields.means: the driver kind to admit, from the one kind list (drivers/kinds.nim) — e.g. 'unanimous'

steps.does: Clicks '＋ Propose <kind>' in the Statement picker, which proposes {effect: 'add-driver', kind} under the compose policy in force. It is schema-bound governance: its bytes can never be read as a payment. The proposal publishes its policy, the effect, and the signing context: environment 'room', account = the room's topic, slot = the intent id, expiry = now + MUSTER_INTENT_TTL_S (7 days by default). The intent id is content-addressed from the effect and the policy.
Endorse it like a statement: dCBOR ['muster.threshold.v1', 'muster.effect.governance.add-driver.v1', {kind}] signed with Ed25519 room identities.
steps.signs: an Ed25519 signature by the member's room identity (their encryption identity's Ed25519 key, held in the keystore) over the materialization: the dCBOR array ['muster.threshold.v1', schema id, {field: value…}] (CDE map order, shortest integers); plus a muster attestation by the same key over P = (context, the materialization, the provenance record)

steps.does: Once the intent is executable, every member's fold of roomDriverKinds adds the kind — once, and only if it is on this client's one kind list. coordinate_drivers then marks it admitted and the composer offers it. coordinate_submit on it answers 'not-onchain': a room family has no settlement, and the card reads '✓ Endorsed — a signed group decision. Nothing settles on-chain.'

refusals.what: admitting a kind while its add-driver is still collecting
refusals.why: a collecting add-driver grants nothing; only an approved one (executable or beyond) admits

refusals.what: admitting a kind this client does not have
refusals.why: roomDriverKinds adds only kinds on the one list — admitting one it lacks would be a guess

refusals.what: a non-member pushing it to approved
refusals.why: a non-roster endorsement never counts, so nothing is admitted

refusals.what: reading an add-driver signature as a transfer
refusals.why: the governance schema separates the bytes (F-5)

actions.ui: Room → + → Statement → '＋ Propose <kind>' (a kind the room has not admitted) → the add-driver card → Approve; the room's Endorse-with buttons then include the kind.

claims.claim: A kind is admitted only by an add-driver intent that reached executable, and only if it is on this client's kind list; a non-member cannot grant it

Which policy approves an add-driver is the proposer's choice: roomDriverKinds admits from ANY executable add-driver intent, whatever its policy — under an Attest policy, one of a Safe's signers is enough
claims.party: the proposer and the members who endorse

claims.claim: Admission is decided in the room and nowhere else
